expected.summary: The board is saved and clean: Layout closes it without saving; it is no longer open.

rows.reason: doc close always closes the one document it names; a document the session does not have open is the not_found row.

expected.summary: --discard is a switch and takes no value.
The session has no such document open.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.

A forward-annotation job on this board has ended, and no job get or job list has read its end yet, so its operation still locks part of the board: E_CONFLICT target_locked, before any confirmation of --discard.
Run under a scope file that does not cover the target (the board); nothing is previewed to the application's files or sent.

While a forward-annotation run or pcb export job of this tool runs in Layout, the session reports busy or unresponsive. Only --session is given: Layout does not say which board it has open while it does not answer, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Layout before the call, such as Setup > Setup Parameters or Help > About. Layout stops answering COM, the session is reported blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a blocked Layout does not say which board it has open.
Layout goes away after Close was sent.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Layout cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: The board holds unsaved changes of this tool and --discard is not given: refused with E_CONFLICT unsaved_changes; nothing closes.

rows.reason: The read-back is whether the board is still open; Layout's close itself checks that the board is gone and fails with E_NATIVE_FAILURE otherwise, so there is no stored value that can differ.
